author: Adrianna Lawrence
title: 'Worst position to be in:' Attorney of Myrtle Beach officer says client saved lives amid mayhem of mass shooting - NewsBreak
text:
By Adrianna Lawrence ,
1 hours ago
MYRTLE BEACH, S.C. (WBTW) — News13 is the first to hear from officer Brandon O’Rourke’s attorney.
The South Carolina Law Enforcement Division on Wednesday released a redacted report detailing the chaotic events surrounding a deadly April 26 officer-involved shooting on N. Ocean Boulevard in Myrtle Beach.
The 40-page report concludes that Myrtle Beach Police Officer Brandon O’Rourke shot and killed 18-year-old Jerrius Davis of Bennettsville after Davis fired four shots from a 40 caliber Taurus handgun into a crowd that included multiple people from Marlboro County.
Two juvenile victims and their families claim they were on Ocean Boulevard that night and were shot by O’Rourke.
His attorney Billy Monckton said he’s not sure if one of O’Rourke’s bullets hit any bystanders but added his client had no other choice than to try and stop Davis.
O’Rourke returned to field work a few weeks ago after 15th circuit solicitor Jimmy Richardson decided to decline prosecution stating O’Rourke was justified in his use of deadly force. O’Rourke was put on administrative duty following the shooting which is standard protocol.
At least two victims and their families News13 have spoken to said they were caught in the crossfire and injured because of O’Rourke’s bullets.
“It’s the worst position any police officers got to be in,” he said. “You know, you can’t let them keep shooting, you’ve got to take immediate action. And if somebody was hit by his weapon, obviously, you know, he’d be extremely remorseful for that. But I haven’t seen any evidence that has been given to us that he did.”
In the 40-page report SLED sent to News13, not one-page details what and whose bullet hit the 11 bystanders.
Civil rights activist John C. Barnett, who represents at least two juvenile victims is concerned his clients have yet to receive closure.
“They can have 40 pages, 80 pages, 120 pages,” Barnett said. “Just show me the page of just one of these particular bullets. If that bullet had struck the ear of our President Donald Trump, they surely would have found out whose bullet it was, whose gun it was, and you know who pulled the trigger.”
News13 asked Monckton about Myrtle Beach Police and SLED’s lack of releasing body and surveillance footage from that night. He said Myrtle Beach could not release anything without SLED’s approval.
“You don’t want to be releasing a bunch of videos because then you basically could be contaminating witnesses because they get to see things that they really didn’t get to see,” he said. “So I understand why SLED did it. I know that there was a uproar in the community about, hey, we want to see everything now, but sometimes it’s not best to see everything now because it’s not completely investigated, but it’s all there now.”
News13 is waiting to receive surveillance video and body camera footage from SLED or the police department. At this time the city or SLED cannot say if officer O’Rourke struck any bystanders.
News13 reached out to Jerrius Davis’s mom for comment but haven’t heard back.
Mayor Brenda Bethune said in a text message she hadn’t read the report yet and wasn’t available for an interview until Thursday. A police spokesperson said any investigation-related questions should be directed to SLED.
